endpoints.reach: Monroe county access to ADM access site
endpoints.endpointName: Columbus Pawnee Park Trail Loup River landing
endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: ne_ngpc_loup_river_trip_planner columbus-water-trail-end: Decimal-degree start and end access-site coordinates transcribed from page 1 of the official Loup River Water Trail trip planner. The text identifies the Monroe Access Point as the public start, describes the downstream trip to Columbus, and publishes Start: 41.461082, -97.599121 / End: 41.418113, -97.367618. The coordinates are retained as access anchors rather than assumed water entries; the workflow derives water-entry coordinates independently from NHD hydrography. The accompanying page 2 map identifies water-access and parking symbols.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (ne_ngpc_loup_river_trip_planner columbus-water-trail-end) on Loup River; treat the agency parking/carry anchor as on/near-water evidence, but confirm the exact water entry and landing before launch.

endpoints.reach: Monroe county access to ADM access site
endpoints.endpointName: ADM access site south of Southeast 9th Street
endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: city_columbus_adm_access_exhibit adm-loup-water-trail-terminal-entry: The City of Columbus lease exhibit outlines the public access corridor from Southeast 9th Street to a unique sand-bank entry beside a wooded parcel. The exhibit is south-up; its rail line, canal, access road, wooded parcel, and braided-bank geometry were aligned to current satellite imagery before selecting the water-side end of the mapped corridor. Nebraska Game and Parks independently identifies this terminal access as lying on the Platte River about one mile downstream from the mouth of the Loup. Fresh candidate-centered NHD queries must verify the Platte River flowline, water polygon, and zero-gap Loup-Platte confluence topology before this map-derived point can be applied.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the exact named authoritative water-entry control (city_columbus_adm_access_exhibit adm-loup-water-trail-terminal-entry) on Platte River; the 402 ft named-flowline offset reflects incomplete or generalized NHD coverage, not a proposed coordinate move.
